findings.finding: H1 FY27 profit is likely below H1 FY26 (underlying EBITDA GBP37.3m) because Q1 group net revenue fell 6.4% and the company has guided the year to an H2 weighting. The market has been told to expect a soft half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26 (20 Nov 2025): EBITDA -0.5% and the GBP100m target pushed out; the stock fell 21.2%, but that move was the guidance line. Q1 FY27 (29 Jul 2026), revenue -6.4% inside guidance: -2.3%.
findings.original_quote: Consistent with our year end guidance, we continue to expect a greater weighting of performance towards the second half of the financial year
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The soft half has been guided since June, so it lands inside the guide. Only a shortfall well beyond the Q1 run-rate would be new, and nothing sourced points to one. If the market feared a large miss, the stock would not have risen 24% since September.
findings.independence: H1 FY26 comparator from the issuer's own interim RNS: https://www.paypointbusiness.com/media/idvjqwkr/h1-fy26-rns-final.pdf

findings.finding: Love2shop lead indicators were strongly up in Q1: billings GBP44.9m vs GBP38.4m (+17%), Love2shop Business +12%, in-store billings +108%, July 'Thank You Teacher' sales value +97%. Billings drive the H2 revenue recognition that the FY guide depends on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 trading update (28 Jan 2026) reported strong Love2shop and parcels peak billings with 'on track for record profits': +14.8%.
findings.original_quote: billings strongly ahead of the prior year at £44.9m (Q1 FY26: £38.4m)
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July. What is new is whether Q2 and Christmas pre-orders kept that pace. Part of the 600p-to-744p rally probably already reflects it, so it is mostly priced. It is net of the rest of the company: Merchant Services (-6.1%) and Network Services parcels (-6.5%) are still shrinking.
findings.independence: Q3 FY26 trading update shows the same seasonal Love2shop billings dynamic: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/gnw/paypoint--pay/trading-update-for-the-three-months-ended-31-/9390142

findings.finding: At the CMD on 29 Sep 2026, one day before the half closed, the board said trading had continued in line with expectations since Q1 and reaffirmed meeting FY27 market expectations and the GBP30m pa buyback to March 2028. That makes reiteration of the guide the base case and lowers the chance of a repeat of last year's interim shock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMD day (29 Sep 2026): +5.0%. Interim with a target push-out (20 Nov 2025): -21.2%. Q3 reaffirmation after that crash: +14.8%.
findings.original_quote: Since the Group's Q1 FY27 Trading Update on 29 July 2026, trading has continued in line with expectations. The Board remains confident in the Group's outlook for FY27 and in meeting market expectations for the year.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock rose 5% that day and kept climbing to 744p. What remains is the residual difference between this year's and last year's interim risk. A plain reiteration at a 24%-higher price is a lower bar to clear than last November's, but not a catalyst.
findings.independence: Same reiteration of FY27 expectations in the FY26 results (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/gnw/paypoint--pay/-record-profits-delivered-and-reorganisation-/9612288) and the 30 Mar outlook.

findings.finding: Q2 parcels has an easier comparator. The H1 FY26 interim said InPost/Yodel harmonisation disruption plus the new contract terms hit the parcels network harder than anticipated in that half, so Q2 FY27 laps a disrupted Q2 FY26. This is an inference; Q1 FY27 parcels were still rebasing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The parcels disruption was part of the -21.2% H1 FY26 reaction.
findings.original_quote: the impact from the disruption to our parcels network from the harmonisation of InPost and Yodel services combined with the commercial terms of our new 3-year contract has been greater than we had anticipated
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only. Q1 FY27 still said the parcel business 'continues to rebase', and the company has not quantified Q2 parcels, so it is not a document-backed number. Small.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 RNS: Royal Mail volumes growing but not yet offsetting InPost: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/gnw/paypoint--pay/1st-quarter-results/9692244

findings.finding: Net corporate debt opened FY27 at GBP132.5m (~1.44x the GBP92.0m EBITDA, against a 1.2-1.5x target). H1 FY26's GBP84.0m was flattered by the GBP43.9m IDS Collect+ investment, while this half carries buybacks, the final dividend and the Aperidata acquisition. The H1 FY27 net debt headline will be much higher year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observed; no clean read of a net-debt surprise on this name.
findings.original_quote: Net corporate debt of £132.5 million increased by £35.1 million as expected from opening position of £97.4 million, reflecting strategic investments and ongoing share buyback programme
findings.why_not_priced: Partly mitigated by the CMD statement that leverage is 'within the Board's target range'. The money buys back about 7% of the market cap a year, so this is not distress. The risk is a headline showing leverage at or above 1.5x on H2-weighted EBITDA, which a cash-sensitive market (cf. Luceco) can sell.
findings.independence: H1 FY26 net debt GBP84.0m and the IDS GBP43.9m investment: https://www.paypointbusiness.com/media/idvjqwkr/h1-fy26-rns-final.pdf ; https://www.conveniencestore.co.uk/news/royal-mail-invests-439m-in-collect-network/710010.article

findings.finding: Exceptional legal costs should fall. The G365 Competition Appeal Tribunal claim (GBP172.2m claimed) was resolved on 7 May 2026 with GBP169k damages, and H1 FY26 adjusting items had carried GBP2.6m of legal costs on these claims. Reorganisation provisions will offset part of that in statutory PBT.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction on this line.
findings.original_quote: Awarded damages of £169,334 plus interest to G365
findings.why_not_priced: Public since May. It sits below underlying profit and has no path to the guide, so it is worth a fraction of operating money.

findings.why_not_priced: Public for five weeks and small. The filing does not state direction or the previous level, so the 'sale' is read from 3.998% < 4%.

baseline_tension: The findings are neutral (sum 0.0) against a mildly positive priced lean (+1.14, mostly the short-squeeze component of a 1.75% quant short that is covering) and a large 60-day run-up (+18.4%). The run-up raises the bar for a reiterating print, so the scaled number leans slightly negative (-0.22) while the findings net to zero. Neither is decisive.
language_note: The UK local half here is the RNS record via Investegate, which carried the CMD's current-trading sentence ('trading has continued in line with expectations', 29 Sep 2026), the Harwood TR-1 dip below 4% and the SIP-only nature of the October PDMR dealings. None of the English wire/aggregator searches (AJ Bell, RTT, Stockopedia, Quartr) surfaced these for the current half.
The domestic convenience-retail trade press (Convenience Store, Asian Trader, Retail Gazette) carried nothing the English sources did not already carry for this window.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': H1-below-prior-year finding cut from -0.4 to -0.2, and CMD in-line finding from +0.3 to +0.2 because it lands inside the guide
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): net-debt headline finding enlarged from -0.2 to -0.3 with a wider downside range

'A narrow proxy loses / inference is a hypothesis': Q2 parcels-comparator inference cut from +0.2 to +0.1; Love2shop billings lead indicator from +0.4 to +0.3 (public since July, net of shrinking Merchant/parcels lines)

'Reiterated or none: median 2.3%' vs 'new numbers 7.4%': abs_move_pct moved from 6.0 to 5.5 because the guide is most likely reiterated for a third time, though the Q2 numbers are new. The size was not capped by the uncertainty about sign

Added the Harwood TR-1 (-0.1) after re-reading the set; it was found in the hunt but left out of the draft. Harwood's 3.998% may reflect a disposal, so the finding is small and was not counted in the draft sum
